narrative.title: Tracing the Courier's Call Sign Across the Switchboard
narrative.scenario: A dispatch switchboard lays out letters in a grid, and a courier's call sign must be traced as a path through adjacent cells — stepping up, down, left, or right without reusing a cell. An operator starts on any cell matching the first letter, marks it taken, and probes onward for each following letter, un-marking on the way back so other routes stay available.
narrative.inputFormat: A grid board of characters and the target string word.
narrative.outputFormat: true when some adjacent-cell path spells word, false otherwise.
constraints: board and word consist of letters and digits

complexity.optimalTime: O(M * N * 4^L) — every cell can seed a walk of L letters

testCases.explanation: The path A→B→C→C→E→D snakes through the left half of the grid.
Reaching B after C would require reusing the starting cell, which the no-revisit rule forbids.

hintLevels: Level 1: The board is a graph of adjacent cells; the word is a self-avoiding walk that must spell it.
Level 2: Match one letter per recursion level: try all four neighbours whose cell equals the next letter, mark the current cell before recursing and restore it after.
Level 3: Marking by overwriting the cell (a sentinel character) avoids a separate visited grid — and restoring it in the same call keeps alternate routes intact.
